extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, IPR parties, PTAB counsel, and USPTO decisionmakers
extracted.subtask_description: A Director Review order resolving an IPR Final Written Decision by evaluating the credibility and consistency of expert testimony, reversing the Board's obviousness finding when that finding rested on contradictory expert evidence, and terminating the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crediting expert testimony must account for credibility findings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board abused its discretion by improperly crediting expert testimony that has multiple material contradictions and that the Board found lacked credibility at least in certain respects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Board finds aspects of an expert's testimony not credible, it cannot properly base a dispositive finding on that testimony without addressing and reconciling those credibility issues. Example: the Board agreed that Mr. Hutton's explanation was "not credible" yet relied on his testimony to find a reason to combine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of expert testimony (no material self-contradiction)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the party with the burden of proof rests its case on an expert’s self-contradictory testimony, the evidence may be insufficient to satisfy that standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contradictory statements (e.g., witness first says an exhibit does not represent a proposed modification, then later says it does) can render the testimony unreliable. Authorities: Finesse Wireless LLC v. AT&T Mobility LLC; Johns Hopkins Univ. v. Datascope Corp. The presence of multiple material contradictions undermines the party's burden of proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centrality of testimony to a finding (e.g., reason to combine)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a particular piece of expert testimony is central to an asserted ground (such as a reason to combine references for obviousness), contradictions in that testimony can invalidate the related finding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the Board rested its finding of a reason to combine on Mr. Hutton’s contradictory testimony — and that testimony was central to Petitioner’s analysis — the Board’s finding of unpatentability on the Szrek-based grounds was reversed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weight accorded to testimony found unreliable on one issue
rubrics_metrics.description: In the determination of litigated facts, the testimony of one who has been found unreliable as to one issue may properly be accorded little weight as to the next.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A credibility determination on one issue justifies giving little or no weight to the same witness's testimony on related or subsequent issues. Authority: N.L.R.B. v. Pittsburgh S.S. Co., 337 U.S. 656, 659 (1949).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on relying on the same unreliable testimony for other grounds not reached
rubrics_metrics.description: Having determined that an expert is not credible as to multiple material aspects of his testimony, it would be inappropriate to rely on that testimony for other grounds the Board did not reach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if the Board did not explicitly rule on other asserted grounds, unreliability in central testimony means those other grounds cannot be sustained on that same testimony; reliance would be improper. The order terminated the proceeding for this reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceeding termination is appropriate when central testimony is unreliable across grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: When central expert testimony is found not credible on multiple material aspects, terminating the IPR proceeding may be appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director terminated the proceeding rather than remanding or leaving other grounds in place. Cited authorities for termination in similar circumstances: Sling TV, L.L.C. v. Realtime Adaptive Streaming LLC; BioDelivery Scis. Int’l, Inc. v. Aquestive Therapeutics, Inc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director Review may reverse Board's Final Written Decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Director Review can be granted and the Director can reverse the Board's Final Written Decision based on abuse of discretion in the Board's factfinding or credibility determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order states: ORDERED that Director Review is granted; FURTHER ORDERED that the Board’s Final Written Decision is reversed; FURTHER ORDERED that the proceeding is terminated.

rubrics_metrics.name: This order is not a Final Written Decision under 35 U.S.C. § 318(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision explicitly states that it does not constitute a final written decision under 35 U.S.C. § 318(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural note for parties: although the Director reversed the Board and terminated the proceeding, this specific order is not a § 318(a) final written decision (affecting any subsequent statutory timelines or appeals analysis).
